caseStudies.ctaDesc: Tell us what is costing you time. We reply within one business day.
caseStudies.cs1Challenge: An operations team managing complex programme delivery was spending over 60% of staff time on manual data entry, report compilation, and cross-referencing records across multiple spreadsheets. The process was error-prone, slow, and preventing the team from focusing on core delivery work.
caseStudies.cs1Solution: We deployed a document processing AI pipeline that automatically extracts, validates, and categorises incoming reports and records. An n8n workflow routes data into the correct Airtable bases and triggers summary reports for programme managers, without any manual intervention.
caseStudies.cs1Result1: 78% reduction in manual data processing time
caseStudies.cs1Result3: Error rate dropped from 8% to under 0.5%
caseStudies.cs1Result4: Programme managers receive auto-generated weekly summaries
caseStudies.cs2Challenge: A mid-sized consulting firm was manually processing client invoices, reconciling expenses, and generating monthly financial reports. Three members of the finance team spent an average of 2 days per month solely on invoice reconciliation. With a growing client base, this was becoming unsustainable.
caseStudies.cs2Solution: We built a fully automated invoice processing system that ingests invoices via email, extracts line items using document AI, validates against purchase orders in their ERP, and posts approved invoices directly to Xero. A Slack notification alerts the finance lead only when human review is required.
caseStudies.cs2Result2: Invoice processing time cut from 2 days to 90 minutes/month
caseStudies.cs2Result3: 94% of invoices processed without human intervention
caseStudies.cs2Result4: Finance team reallocated to higher-value client work
caseStudies.cs3Challenge: A logistics operation was losing competitive advantage due to a slow invoicing cycle. Invoices were manually compiled from multiple driver reports, fuel logs, and delivery confirmations, a process taking 3 full working days per billing cycle. Late invoices were causing cash flow problems and client dissatisfaction.
caseStudies.cs3Solution: We integrated all data sources, driver apps, GPS systems, fuel cards, and delivery confirmation data, into a unified pipeline. An AI agent compiles draft invoices automatically, flags exceptions, and sends approved invoices to clients via the existing billing system. The entire cycle now runs overnight.
caseStudies.cs3Result1: Invoice cycle compressed from 3 days to 4 hours
caseStudies.cs3Result2: Cash flow improved by approximately 18 days per quarter
caseStudies.cs3Result3: Zero manual compilation for 91% of invoices

about.metaDesc: Fifteen years of being responsible for systems businesses had to rely on. Maxpromo Digital came out of that.
about.title: Fifteen years of being responsible when it had to keep running.
about.intro: Maxpromo Digital designs and builds the systems companies run on, and keeps running them afterwards. The second part is what decides whether the first part was worth doing.
about.storyBody: Joomla, WordPress, Drupal and TYPO3. Shared hosting and self-managed servers. SQL, migrations, backups and the imports that go wrong at two in the morning. Fifteen years of that is what informs how we build now: cautiously, with a way back, and with someone responsible when it breaks.
about.transformTitle: Most businesses do not need another website.
about.transformBody: They need the tools they already pay for to talk to each other. They need the manual steps gone. They need the old system brought up to a state somebody can work with. A rebuild is sometimes the answer. More often it is the expensive way to avoid a smaller and less comfortable question about how the work moves.

principles.d: We do not start from a technology and look for somewhere to put it. We start from what is costing time and work back.
A smaller system a team actually uses beats a larger one that impresses in a demo and is abandoned by March.

principles.t: A person stays in the loop
principles.d: Anything that leaves the business is drafted and approved. Automation prepares work. It does not act on your behalf unsupervised.
A system nobody maintains decays. We keep running what we build, or hand it over properly to someone who will.

about.arcLede: Nobody starts out designing operating systems for businesses. You end up there after being the person answerable for whether something kept working.
about.a1Body: Production environments, databases, migrations, hosting, integrations. An import that went wrong at two in the morning and a business that has to trade again by nine. Years of that, for real companies with real customers.
about.a2Body: Almost never at the technology. Systems break at the edges: where information gets carried from one place to the next, where nobody owns the handover, where one person holds it all in their head and then takes a holiday.
about.a3Body: Once you know where it breaks, the question changes. It stops being which tool, and becomes how does the work actually run here, and which of these steps should not need to exist.
about.a4Body: That is what Maxpromo Digital became. We design the route work takes through a company and build the systems that carry it. A business should get easier to run as it grows, not harder.

capabilities.c1Does: We record how the work actually runs, remove the steps nobody needs, and let a workflow carry the rest. Follow-ups, reminders, approvals and documents happen without anyone having to remember them.
capabilities.c2Pain: The off-the-shelf tool does not fit, and the spreadsheet beside it became the real system.
capabilities.c2Does: We build the application around the process your business actually has: internal tools, portals, dashboards, interfaces for staff and customers. Not a template you have to bend yourself around.
capabilities.c3Pain: The website brings enquiries, and then the manual work starts again.

capabilities.c4Does: Preparing, creating, approving, publishing and tracking as one route instead of five separate jobs. Images, video and copy run through the same controlled path.

capabilities.c5Does: Data, copy and assets come together into one product record, and the channels read from it. Maintenance happens once rather than four times.

whatWeDo.title: We start with what is slowing the business down, not with what we sell.
whatWeDo.lede: Most companies do not arrive knowing whether they need an automation, an application or a better connection between two systems they already pay for. That is a reasonable place to be. Working it out is our job, and it is the first thing we do.
whatWeDo.diffTitle: The right answer depends on where the work is actually getting stuck.
whatWeDo.d1: Sometimes the work is more complicated than it needs to be, and the honest answer is to simplify it before anything gets built.
whatWeDo.d2: Sometimes the tools are fine and simply do not talk to each other, so people move the information by hand.
whatWeDo.d3: Sometimes a handful of steps repeat every day and should be carrying themselves.
whatWeDo.d4: Sometimes a process has outgrown its spreadsheet and needs an application built around it.
whatWeDo.d5: Sometimes the website should be doing part of the work instead of only showing information.

capabilityPages.c1m2Body: It reaches the right person or the right system without being forwarded by hand.
capabilityPages.c1m3Body: Documents, replies and records are drafted from what is already known.
capabilityPages.c1m4Body: What happened is written down where the business can find it later.
capabilityPages.c1m5Title: Leave the decision with a person
capabilityPages.c1m5Body: Anything that commits the business to something waits for somebody to approve it.
capabilityPages.c1BeforeA11y: Before: an enquiry arrives and is handled by five separate manual steps, with information copied between them and no single record.
capabilityPages.c1AfterA11y: After: the enquiry is captured once, routed automatically, prepared for a person to approve, and recorded in one place.
capabilityPages.c1HumanTitle: The system does the carrying. People still decide.
capabilityPages.c1HumanBody: A quote going out, a price being agreed, an exception to the usual rule. Those stay with the person whose job they are. What changes is that the work arrives ready for the decision instead of needing to be assembled first.
capabilityPages.c1CtaBody: The part of the week that feels like typing rather than working is usually the right place to start.
capabilityPages.c2Title: When spreadsheets and off-the-shelf software stop fitting.
capabilityPages.c2Lede: Most businesses do not outgrow their software all at once. It happens gradually, and the signs are familiar long before anyone calls it a problem.
capabilityPages.c2FamiliarTitle: The software is still in use, and so are the workarounds.
capabilityPages.c2FamiliarLede: Again, not all of these. Two of them is usually enough to be worth a conversation.
capabilityPages.c2f1: There are more spreadsheets than anyone can name, and some of them matter.
capabilityPages.c2f2: An important process lives mostly in one person's head.
capabilityPages.c2f3: Staff have quiet workarounds for the software they were given.
capabilityPages.c2f4: The same information exists in three places and disagrees in at least one.
capabilityPages.c2f5: The tool technically supports the task, but only through steps nobody would design.
capabilityPages.c2f6: Customers or staff need one focused place to do a thing, and there isn't one.
capabilityPages.c2HonestTitle: Custom software is not automatically the better answer.
capabilityPages.c2HonestBody: It is more to build, more to look after and more to get wrong. Often the right move is to connect the systems you already have, or to use more of what you already pay for. We will say so when that is the case, and it costs you less than the alternative.
capabilityPages.c2HonestClose: Building something new is worth it when the process is genuinely yours, and the software you can buy is built for a different business.
capabilityPages.c2BuildTitle: One focused place where the work actually happens.
capabilityPages.c2b1Body: The screen your team works in all day, built around the process they actually follow.
capabilityPages.c2b2Body: A place for customers, suppliers or staff to do one thing without an email thread.
capabilityPages.c2b3Body: Jobs, records, approvals and status in one place instead of four.
capabilityPages.c2b4Body: A front end for an automated process, so people can see it and step in.
capabilityPages.c2HumanTitle: Built around how your team already works.
capabilityPages.c2HumanBody: An application that forces a new way of working gets abandoned, and the spreadsheets come back. We start from what people do now, keep the parts that work, and only change what is causing the trouble.
capabilityPages.c2CtaTitle: Tell us what you have outgrown.
capabilityPages.c2CtaBody: Usually there is one process everybody complains about. That is the one to describe.
